notes: Draft 3. The v2 script narrated what the picture already showed, which served Execution and left Potential Impact unscored and 'how you used WebMCP' -- an explicit rule requirement -- barely covered. This one spends its first 40 seconds on what Mathburst is, the problem it solves, and how WebMCP is actually wired in, and pays for it by cutting the play-by-play roughly in half. Target: 2:52 picture, about 2:20 of speech, so the demo can breathe. Each clip now names the shot it plays over and its offset within that shot, so the spec is the single source for the words and the manifest owns only timing, steps and camera. 13-simplex was dropped with the simplex scene.

clips.text: This is Mathburst. An infinite canvas where a student and an AI tutor do mathematics inside the same document.
Today a tutor can only talk about your work. Your actual reasoning is trapped in a photograph, or a canvas it has no way to reach. So it explains around the problem instead of touching it.

Mathburst registers forty-eight WebMCP tools on the page itself. The tutor calls them the way you use the toolbar: the same reducer, the same history. Every edit it makes is attributed, visible, and undoable.
The student writes the Gamma recurrence by hand. The sign error is deliberate.
The tutor reads the ink and circles exactly where integration by parts flips the sign. It marks. It does not fix.
The student corrects it. Then the tutor types LaTeX into a live equation and resizes it, using the same handles you would drag.
It pans down and builds the density from nothing. Axes, then the curve, then the area, split into three masses.
Drag the shape and the masses follow. Log masses, then softmax. The same three numbers, arrived at twice.
Which is the bridge to attention. The tutor raises one entry of W Q and explains while the weights move, and they still sum to one.
One gradient step by the tutor, undone. Then eight by the student. Every click is real arithmetic on the parameters you can see.
The student places three points. Tangent circles, the homothety and the spiral centre construct themselves in dependency order.
P is a weighted average of A, B and C. Weights that sum to one, like attention weights. So P glides to them.
Ramanujan's congruence, verified for these finite cases. The card says plainly that the general statement is a theorem, and not one proved here.
A matrix typed by hand, sheared by tool. One matrix moves every vector at once.
A second project opens, untouched. Isolation, on camera.
Forty-eight tools, every one of them used, through one shared history. [calm] A tutor that can enter the work instead of describing it. One mathematical world. Every agent can enter.
